A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IOPO method and TRACE benchmark. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison, including the derivation moved from v1 Appendix E to v3 Appendix G.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations on TRACE, IFEval and CFBench, including preference-component ablations, token-budget comparisons and resource measurements.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds ComplexBench results, additional comparison methods, mainstream-model evaluations and results for a simplified IOPO variant.

M1.justification: V3 Appendix E introduces an optional reduced IOPO objective that omits the second preference component, using fewer input-output pairs to reduce memory requirements. The main IOPO procedure remains intact; its reformulation in Equations 9–10 is algebraically equivalent to v1.

E1.justification: V3 adds evaluation on ComplexBench, comprising 1,150 examples covering constraint composition. This extends coverage within the existing complex-instruction-following task. TRACE, IFEval and CFBench remain, with unchanged TRACE training and evaluation populations.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds ORPO and SimPO for both model backbones alongside the retained Instruct, SFT, PPO and DPO comparisons. SimPO was discussed but not evaluated in v1. New Appendix F/Table 7 additionally evaluates OpenAI o1, DeepSeek-R1 (671B) and Claude-3.5-Sonnet, substantially broadening the comparator set.

E3.justification: V3 adds ComplexBench evaluation using the decomposed requirements following ratio, DRFR. The retained benchmarks' metrics, TRACE splits, backbone models and principal training settings remain unchanged. Calling the per-GPU batch size a micro batch size clarifies documentation without establishing a changed training budget.

E4.justification: Table 4 extends the existing input/output preference ablations to ComplexBench. Appendix E adds a memory-versus-performance assessment of the reduced objective. The original resource analysis and matched-token comparisons in Table 5 and Figures 4–5 are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same quality audit of 100 instructions by three annotators, with 95% agreement. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests for the model comparisons.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial results for new comparators and ComplexBench; IOPO scores 72.6 and 71.8 DRFR versus DPO's 70.9 and 70.8 for the two backbones. Table 7 adds the consistent ranking Claude-3.5-Sonnet > o1 > DeepSeek-R1. Appendix E reports approximately 1.5 times DPO's memory usage and a 2.03% average advantage for the reduced variant. All matched entries in Tables 3–4 and the original Table 5 measurements remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix E adds a formal definition of the reduced objective in Equation 11. The original Bradley–Terry construction and derivation remain unchanged in Appendix G. The main loss decomposition and clarification of appendix notation restate existing mathematics; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central TRACE and joint input-output optimization contributions remain. The abstract revises the claimed out-of-domain gains over SFT/DPO from 6.29%/3.13% to 5.91%/2.83%, and the introduction revises overall gains from 7.22%/2.66% to 7.03%/2.51%. These are limited quantitative claim updates reflecting expanded evaluation coverage.

C2.justification: New Appendix F interprets agreement in mainstream-model rankings across benchmarks as evidence of TRACE's quality and argues that IOPO narrows the gap between small and larger models. Appendix E introduces a practical memory-performance tradeoff. The original constraint-awareness explanation and limitation concerning unverified training data remain.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code/data release statement and repository address, explicit ablation losses, and documentation of a final group-pair rationality check. Appendix B removes the worked construction and judging demonstrations, replacing them with abbreviated templates or example placeholders, and omits the separately listed response-generation template. This substantially changes the available reproducibility documentation without establishing that the original experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: V3 adds discussion of ORPO and citations concerning LLM judging, newer comparison models and background applications. The central positioning against output-only preference optimization remains unchanged. ComplexBench's underlying work by Wen et al. was already cited in v1; its evaluation is newly added.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized prose edits, corrects the introduction's Figure 3 references to Figure 1, and clarifies the loss explanation. It reorganizes prompts into B.1–B.5, adds acknowledgements and inserts two appendices before the retained derivation. The main seven-section narrative is preserved.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces detailed examples with a compact schematic, and Figures 2, 6 and 7 are redrawn. Tables 3–4 gain rows or columns, while new Table 7 redisplays the main comparisons alongside mainstream models. The taxonomy table and prompt boxes are substantially compressed, and the final derivation is rotated, producing extensive visual and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The additional ORPO/SimPO comparisons and ComplexBench evaluation strengthen v1's empirical case, while explicit ablation losses, the reduced variant and release information improve clarity and practical usefulness. These gains are limited by the removal of worked prompt examples and a new reporting inconsistency: v3's abstract gives a 2.83% out-of-domain advantage over DPO, but its conclusion retains v1's 3.13%. Overall, the evidence supports a modest quality improvement.
